lines.text: In the world's deepest hole, the drill bit cut rock for less than two minutes in an hour.
lines.cue: caption: UNDER 2 MIN OF CUTTING PER HOUR

lines.text: That's an average, past ten kilometres down.
Near the top, it was about a fifth of the time.
At one stage, the hole went down about a kilometre in six years.
That's under half a metre a day. About two hole-widths.
As one report put it, each extra metre got harder.
So what was the drill doing the rest of the time?
The full video shows where the hour went.
lines.cue: caption: WHERE DID THE HOUR GO?
